scope: Proposition 13.3 (Extraction and allocation) of the manuscript “The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order” (preprints/The-hypercube-Ramsey-number-has-linear-order-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 171 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7d4b26e897038267), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 114. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are pairwise disjoint patches (Xi, Yi) with |Xi| = |Yi| = Mi and P i Mi = S ≥ c N for a fixed c > 0, all of one mode, orientation and color. They have one of the three patch types just specified. A subcollection admits dyadic prefix lengths ℓi with X i 2−ℓi = 1, Mi/S ≤ 2−ℓi < 2Mi/S. In its prefix allocation, patch i has Θ(2nMi/N) roles of each parity. Each star in that patch has exactly ℓi crossing flips, visiting distinct other leaves, and a nested tail coordinate set of size hi supplies its internal directions. Eventually maxi(hi, ℓi) < nι. Except in the bounded case, ℓi, log(N/Mi) ≤ si/(1000u). The bounded case uses one patch, with ℓi = hi = si = 0.
